families.title: Grounding Spatial Relations in a Compact World Model: Instruction Leakage and a Goal-Free Dynamics Fix
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: arXiv:2607.06925v1#S3 — compact action-conditioned world-model formulation and goal-conditioned baseline
arXiv:2607.06925v1#S4 — instruction-leakage diagnosis and goal-free dynamics intervention
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.06925v1#S5.SS1 — controlled spatial-relation tasks and leakage controls
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.06925v1#S5.SS4 — goal-free comparison
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.06925v1#S6 — interpretation of grounding and planner/dynamics separation
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.06925v1#S7 — compact synthetic environment, narrow relation vocabulary and no large-scale physical deployment
families.artifact_locator: No official event-time repository or uniquely versioned artifact is disclosed in exact v1; formulas, task construction and reported tables are manuscript evidence only.
families.mechanism_summary: The baseline gives the transition model both the current scene/action and an instruction that directly names the spatial relation later used as the evaluation target. The model can therefore copy goal semantics rather than infer the environment transition. Removing goal identity from dynamics and keeping it in the planner's objective forces the learned transition to explain observation changes instead of receiving the answer-bearing variable.
families.state_and_flow: The environment owns observation and transition truth; the dynamics model owns an action-conditioned next-state estimate; the planner owns the goal and cost. The fix moves goal identity out of the transition data path, so success evidence must flow from predicted state through an independently applied objective rather than from instruction text into the scored relation.

benchmark_contract.workload: compact spatial-relation prediction under instruction-conditioned and goal-free variants
benchmark_contract.models: paper-defined compact world-model variants; parameter count Not Disclosed in the reportable contract
benchmark_contract.length: short controlled trajectories; exact production horizon Not Applicable
benchmark_contract.slo: No serving SLO; evaluates prediction/grounding behavior
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author-defined spatial-relation tasks with leakage and withheld-goal controls
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: The intervention identifies one leakage channel in a compact controlled setup. It does not prove that every goal-conditioned world model is ungrounded or that goal-free dynamics alone produces causal physical understanding.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports the causal concern that an answer-bearing instruction can let a dynamics model bypass transition learning, and that removing the goal improves the controlled grounding test. It does not establish general physical-world causality, long-horizon planning or deployment safety.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch25 separates video continuation from action-conditioned environment dynamics and hands planning to downstream policy, but it does not make instruction leakage an explicit authority failure.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds a durable design test: when the instruction names the scored state variable, goal-conditioned dynamics may solve the metric without learning the transition. Goal identity should normally remain planner cost, while dynamics owns only state-transition evidence.
books_review.suggested_patch: After the action-conditioned transition contract, add an instruction-leakage subsection: preserve goal-conditioned dynamics where goal variables are genuine environment inputs, but exclude answer-bearing goals when the purpose is to test grounded transition learning. Require withheld/counterfactual goal controls and state that goal-free dynamics trades task-specific efficiency for a more honest grounding test.

families.title: UP: Unbounded Positive Asymmetric Optimization for Breaking the Exploration-Stability Dilemma
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; PDF used because exact-v1 HTML was unavailable
method_locators: arXiv:2607.06987v1 PDF §4.1-§4.2 — self-anchored positive ratio, stop-gradient denominator and asymmetric negative clipping
arXiv:2607.06987v1 PDF Appendix A — gradient derivation and relation to GRPO/DAPO/GSPO
evaluation_locators: arXiv:2607.06987v1 PDF §5.1-§5.5 — model/task contract, optimizer variants, probability-capacity analysis and ablations
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.06987v1 PDF §6 and experiment disclosures — author results are bounded to listed Qwen families and math/geometry regimes; no universal stability proof
families.artifact_locator: Project page https://chongyu-fan.netlify.app/posts/up/ is disclosed; no uniquely identified public code repository or event-time commit is disclosed, so implementation equivalence is Not Verified.
families.mechanism_summary: For positive advantages, UP replaces the stale rollout ratio with πθ divided by a stop-gradient copy of itself. Its forward value is one while its gradient is the current-policy REINFORCE gradient, so the positive branch no longer hits the usual upper clipping ceiling. The negative branch retains a conventional bounded ratio/KL safeguard, making the change asymmetric rather than removing stability controls globally.
families.state_and_flow: The rollout policy still owns sampled actions and logged advantages; the learner owns current logits. Stop-gradient makes the current probability an anchor for the forward objective but not a second gradient path. Positive evidence flows through an unclipped current-policy gradient, while negative updates remain governed by the selected GRPO/DAPO/GSPO stability contract.

benchmark_contract.workload: reasoning post-training on mathematical and geometry tasks
benchmark_contract.models: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-8B variants
benchmark_contract.hardware: NVIDIA A100 GPUs where disclosed; exact GPU count varies by run and is not fully normalized
benchmark_contract.precision: training precision Not Disclosed consistently across all runs
benchmark_contract.length: task-dependent reasoning trajectories; exact prompt/output distribution Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.batch: algorithm/run-specific and not fully normalized in the paper tables
benchmark_contract.concurrency: verl/vLLM rollout pipeline; exact global rollout concurrency Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.slo: No serving SLO; reports training reward and benchmark accuracy
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author benchmark harness for mathematics and Geometry3K-style tasks
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: The evidence supports one asymmetric update branch on listed Qwen/task contracts. It does not prove that removing the positive clip is safe for every reward model, policy scale or off-policy delay.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 proves the algebraic gradient contract and reports consistent gains in its experiments. It does not provide a general convergence theorem, public implementation equivalence or evidence outside the evaluated reasoning families.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch33 explains ratio clipping, DAPO-style asymmetric pressures and the exploration/stability trade-off, but still treats both ratio sides as variants of one stale-policy ratio.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds a distinct branch that removes the positive ratio's probability-capacity ceiling without discarding negative-update safeguards. It clarifies that exploration capacity and harmful-update containment need not share one clipping rule.
books_review.suggested_patch: After the clipping discussion, add an asymmetric positive-update branch. Derive the self-anchored ratio and state that forward equality to one does not imply zero gradient because the denominator is stop-gradient. Preserve symmetric clipping as the simpler stability baseline; explain UP's benefit for low-probability positive actions, its extra tail/variance risk, and the need to retain negative clipping, KL and freshness controls.

families.title: Voltron: Enabling Elastic Multi-Device Execution of LLM Inference for Empowered Edge Intelligence
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07046v1#S3 — per-layer MP/TP planning and task-aware precision
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07046v1#S4 — prefill/decode separation and elastic runtime controller
evaluation_locators: arXiv:2607.07046v1#S5 — six-device/three-cluster evaluation, model/task suites, trace replay and QoS thresholds
arXiv:2607.07046v1#S6 — component and adaptation ablations
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07046v1#S7 — edge-cluster/network scope and workload-specific planning limitations
families.artifact_locator: No official event-time source repository or uniquely versioned implementation artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: Voltron first builds distinct per-layer execution plans for prefill and decode, choosing model/tensor parallel placement and precision according to layer/task sensitivity. At runtime it observes memory, KV growth and wireless conditions, then revises device participation, precision and pruning at token boundaries while preloading the next plan to hide reconfiguration.
families.state_and_flow: The planner owns a versioned layer/phase execution plan; devices own weights, KV shards and local capacity; the runtime controller owns boundary-safe revisions under QoS. Prefill activations and decode/KV data follow different device graphs, while monitoring signals affect control state rather than silently mutating committed tokens.

benchmark_contract.workload: interactive edge LLM inference with prefill/decode and LMSYS-derived arrival traces
benchmark_contract.hardware: six heterogeneous edge devices arranged into three measured clusters; exact device inventory is bound to paper §5 tables
benchmark_contract.precision: mixed precision selected per layer/task; exact formats are experiment-specific
benchmark_contract.length: prompt/output distributions follow paper workloads; individual normalized lengths Not Disclosed for every table
benchmark_contract.batch: dynamic request workload; per-table batch Not Disclosed consistently
benchmark_contract.concurrency: trace-driven multi-request execution across participating devices
benchmark_contract.slo: TTFT 10 s and TPOT 400 ms thresholds in the reported QoS contract
benchmark_contract.evaluator: MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM8K and MATH plus measured latency/QoS
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Author measurements depend on the six-device wireless topology and planner cost model. They do not establish universal speedups or safe runtime repartition on unrelated devices/networks.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports phase-specific, per-layer planning and boundary-safe runtime adaptation on its edge setup. It does not prove datacenter-scale behavior, arbitrary-network stability or that mixed precision preserves every task outside the measured evaluator set.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch49 owns compilation and execution-plan decisions, while Ch56 owns fleet admission/routing. Current text mostly treats precision and partitioning as build-time or deployment-time choices.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds an edge branch where the execution plan is versioned and revisable at phase/token boundaries as KV, memory and network conditions change. Precision becomes one control variable inside the plan rather than only an offline artifact property.
books_review.suggested_patch: Add a runtime-revisable execution-plan branch after static build profiles. Separate prefill and decode plans; bind every revision to a token/phase boundary and preserve a committed-token invariant. Hand admission and fleet routing to Ch56. Keep static plans as the valid branch when topology is stable, certification matters or replan overhead exceeds elasticity benefit.

families.title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07144v1#S2 — contractive iterated-map encoding
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07144v1#S3 — anchors and random access
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07144v1#S4 — residual VQ and asymmetric K-V allocation
evaluation_locators: arXiv:2607.07144v1#S6 — reconstruction, suffix retrieval and storage experiments
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07144v1#S7 — GPT-2-scale, 1024-context, one-corpus and CPU-only limitations
families.artifact_locator: https://github.com/eighteight/fractal-kv is linked by the manuscript, but GitHub history contains no commit at or before the Daily window cutoff; event-time implementation provenance is therefore Not Verified.
families.mechanism_summary: A lossy feed quantizer first maps KV into symbol codes; a contractive symbolic map then serializes that quantized code stream into an archive with periodic anchors. The archive is lossless only relative to the codes, supports append and position access without decoding the whole prefix, and can serve as a structural suffix-similarity index. It does not reconstruct the original FP16 KV without quantization error.
families.state_and_flow: The live serving engine owns active KV; the archive owns an append-only recoverable representation and anchors; the structural index owns suffix coordinates, not semantic truth. Rehydration moves archived state back to live KV, and retrieval candidates must still be validated before becoming request context.

benchmark_contract.workload: lossless archival of an already-quantized KV symbol stream and suffix retrieval on a public-domain text corpus
benchmark_contract.hardware: single CPU; exact SKU Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.precision: paper-defined quantized archive; live model precision Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.concurrency: single-process measurements; serving concurrency Not Evaluated
benchmark_contract.slo: No production SLO; storage, reconstruction and access metrics
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author reconstruction and structural suffix-search tests
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Results do not establish semantic retrieval quality, GPU-serving throughput, long-context model accuracy or superiority over concurrent KV quantizers.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports lossless reconstruction of the already-quantized symbol stream, not lossless recovery of original FP16 KV; the feed quantizer incurs the paper-reported quality cost. Structural suffix similarity is not semantic relevance, and the paper does not demonstrate end-to-end production serving gains.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch45 covers live KV identity, paging, tiering, quantization and recomputation, but not a recoverable symbolic archive that also exposes a structural index.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Separates lossy KV-to-code quantization from lossless code-stream archival and from semantic retrieval: the random-access archive may rehydrate quantized KV codes and provide suffix candidates without preserving original FP16 KV or becoming the authority for relevance.
books_review.suggested_patch: Within the cold-tier branch, add recoverable symbolic archives as an experimental alternative to raw KV, lossy quantization and recomputation. Preserve anchors/version/model identity, distinguish structural suffix lookup from semantic retrieval, and state the small CPU experiment boundary. Keep ordinary paging as the default where hot reuse and low decode latency dominate.

families.title: Sparse Delta Memory: Scaling the State of Linear RNNs through Sparsity
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07386v1#S3 — explicit N-slot table and product-key sparse read/write
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07386v1#S4 — gated delta update
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07386v1#S5 — iso-FLOP scaling and language/long-context tasks
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07386v1#S6 — kernel and memory profiling; Appendix A-E
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07386v1#S7 and Appendix F — HBM residence, large physical state, current kernel overhead and limited serving evidence
families.artifact_locator: https://github.com/facebookresearch/sparse-delta-memory and https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention are disclosed, but neither provides a paper-specific event-time commit at or before the window cutoff; artifact equivalence is Not Verified.
families.mechanism_summary: Sparse Delta Memory replaces a fixed dense recurrent matrix with an explicit N-by-d memory table. Product keys choose a small write set and read set, and a gated delta rule changes only selected slots. Increasing N expands addressable state without increasing per-token arithmetic proportionally, but the physical table grows and leaves fast on-chip memory.
families.state_and_flow: Learned initial memory M0 belongs to model parameters; evolving Mt belongs to sequence/request state. The router owns sparse addresses, the delta rule owns selected-slot mutation, and untouched slots retain their previous value. Checkpoint and serving systems must not confuse parameter initialization with per-request recurrent state.

benchmark_contract.workload: iso-FLOP language modeling and long-context retrieval/understanding
benchmark_contract.hardware: GPU experiments reported by authors; exact SKU varies and is not normalized across every table
benchmark_contract.length: training tokens normalized by 160 tokens-per-parameter; RULER and paper long-context lengths
benchmark_contract.concurrency: single-model kernel and end-to-end measurements; online request concurrency Not Evaluated
benchmark_contract.slo: No production SLO; loss, downstream accuracy, throughput and memory
benchmark_contract.evaluator: iso-FLOP language modeling suite, RULER and author kernel profiling
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Constant sparse arithmetic is not constant physical cost. The 8B implementation is reported 1.49x slower end-to-end than the compared GDN path, and the state may approach parameter scale.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports scalable addressable recurrent state and reports quality gains under its iso-FLOP contract. It does not prove that current kernels beat attention/GDN in production serving or that large state can remain cheaply resident.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch22 introduces Gated DeltaNet and recurrent fast-memory alternatives, but its fixed matrix makes capacity and arithmetic grow together conceptually.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds sparse explicit slots: addressable state can scale faster than per-token selected work, while physical HBM, session identity and checkpoint cost become the next bottleneck.
books_review.suggested_patch: After the fixed-matrix delta-memory branch, add sparse explicit slots with product-key routing and selected-slot delta updates. Separate learned M0 from request Mt; state that sparse FLOPs do not remove HBM/storage/checkpoint costs. Keep dense GDN as the valid branch when the state fits fast memory or predictable kernels matter more than capacity.

families.title: Length Penalties Make Chain-of-Thought Less Monitorable
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; submitted in this window despite larger arXiv sequence number
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09786v1#S3 — RL length-penalty intervention
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09786v1#S4 — monitorability probes and content-blind matched shortening controls
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09786v1#S5 — Qwen/Nemotron runs and reasoning benchmarks
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.09786v1#S7 — hint disclosure and judge analyses; Appendix A-D
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.09786v1#S8 and Appendix E — limited seeds/models, diagnostic subsets and evaluator dependence
families.artifact_locator: No official event-time repository or uniquely versioned training artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: A reward penalty for long reasoning traces does more than compress tokens: it can preferentially remove explicit intermediate hints that make a correct answer externally inspectable. Matched content-blind shortening separates mere length reduction from policy adaptation, showing monitorability is an independent objective rather than a guaranteed by-product of concise reasoning.
families.state_and_flow: The post-training objective owns the pressure on emitted reasoning length; the policy owns which intermediate evidence survives; the monitor/evaluator owns observed disclosure, not hidden cognition. A release gate must measure answer quality and evidence visibility separately.

benchmark_contract.workload: RL post-training with length penalties on mathematical/reasoning tasks
benchmark_contract.models: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-14B and a Nemotron 9B check
benchmark_contract.hardware: two NVIDIA B200 GPUs per reported run
benchmark_contract.length: penalized chain-of-thought length; prompt/output distributions are task-specific
benchmark_contract.slo: No serving SLO; evaluates accuracy and monitorability/disclosure
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author probes plus judge rescoring on a limited subset
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Some diagnostics are single-seed and judge rescoring is not uniform across datasets. The paper does not establish a universal monitorability loss for every compression objective.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports a monitorability regression in listed training/evaluation contracts and controls for random shortening. It does not prove that visible CoT is faithful internal reasoning or that all length optimization is unsafe.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch66 already requires multidimensional evaluation and warns that answer accuracy does not establish process faithfulness or monitorability.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Provides a strong but still narrow experimental case that a seemingly benign efficiency reward can degrade visible evidence independently of correctness.
books_review.suggested_patch: No mechanism-body change now. Retain as a Weekly experimental case until replicated across objectives/models with a stable monitorability metric. If later integrated, attach it to release-gate metric coupling rather than treating visible CoT as ground truth.

families.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S3.SS1 — direct two-sided importance correction
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S3.SS2 — trust mask and single-rollout critic
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S4 — asynchronous actor/learner pipeline and update protocol
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S5 — agentic math/SWE tasks and throughput
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07508v1#S6 — algorithm ablations
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07508v1#A2 — critic/rollout-cost assumptions, task scope and asynchronous staleness limits
families.artifact_locator: No official public repository or uniquely versioned event-time artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: SAO uses one rollout per prompt, trains a value critic more frequently than the actor and corrects current-policy learning directly against the rollout policy. Tokens whose two-sided importance ratio leaves a trust interval are masked rather than allowed to dominate. This trades group-relative variance reduction for lower rollout cost and explicit staleness control.
families.state_and_flow: Actors own trajectory policy version and logged behavior probability; the rollout store owns immutable trajectories; the critic owns value estimates; the learner owns current policy and trust-mask decisions. Policy-version identity must survive the asynchronous queue so current-to-rollout correction is computed against the actual generator.

benchmark_contract.workload: agentic RL on tool-using math and SWE-bench-style tasks
benchmark_contract.hardware: accelerator topology Not Disclosed sufficiently for normalized throughput comparison
benchmark_contract.length: maximum context 128k; up to 50 and 300 environment turns in listed regimes
benchmark_contract.concurrency: asynchronous rollout generation and learner updates; exact worker count Not Disclosed
benchmark_contract.slo: No serving SLO; sample efficiency, training throughput and task success
benchmark_contract.evaluator: agentic math and SWE-bench-related evaluation, means over 16 or 4 runs as specified
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: The method depends on critic quality, behavior-probability integrity and bounded staleness. It does not eliminate off-policy failure or prove one rollout is sufficient for arbitrary sparse-reward agents.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports the single-rollout/critic and direct importance-correction design plus bounded task gains. It does not establish universal sample-efficiency gains or production correctness under arbitrary actor lag.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch32 already owns the critic-stability branch; Ch33 already states rollout-policy identity, bounded freshness and one-rollout/asynchronous alternatives with explicit off-policy correction.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: The exact-v1 audit strengthens provenance and benchmark boundaries but does not add a missing durable proposition beyond the existing critic/freshness lifecycle.
books_review.suggested_patch: No body patch. Keep the source in Review notes for the single-rollout branch and preserve policy-version, behavior-probability, critic and trust-mask prerequisites.

method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07534v1#S2 — causal chunk generation
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07534v1#S3 — interaction conditioning

families.mechanism_summary: The system streams causally generated video chunks conditioned on user interactions, then uses few-step distillation and a runtime harness to sustain low-latency continuation. families.state_and_flow: The generator owns the next visual chunk; the interaction loop owns recent action/context; the renderer owns displayed frames. No independent persistent world-state authority guarantees that revisiting a location recovers the same object identity, so visual continuation must not be confused with a revisable simulator state.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 and event-time code support an interactive generation pipeline and author-reported runtime. They do not establish a canonical persistent world, physical correctness or independent benchmark superiority.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch25 already distinguishes indefinitely generated observations from a persistent, revisable environment state and explicitly notes regeneration on revisit as a weaker contract.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: The exact-v1 audit supplies a bounded implementation case but no uncovered durable mechanism.
books_review.suggested_patch: No body patch. Preserve as a Review-notes case for the boundary between streaming video continuation and persistent world state.

families.title: LaMem-VLA: Dual Latent Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07608v1#S3 — short/long latent vaults and latent curator
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07608v1#S4 — memory-action weaving
evaluation_locators: arXiv:2607.07608v1#S5 — SimplerEnv-Bridge/LIBERO evaluation and component ablations
limitations_locators: No dedicated limitations section; exact v1 leaves physical deployment, memory reset/contamination and safety-controller interaction under-evaluated
families.artifact_locator: No official source repository, checkpoint or uniquely versioned event-time artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: LaMem-VLA keeps a short latent vault for immediate task progress and a compressed long vault for older observations, with a curator deciding what moves between them. Memory tokens are woven into action prediction rather than retrieved as text, giving the policy an internal state estimate across partially observed manipulation trajectories.
families.state_and_flow: The VLA policy owns latent task state; the curator owns retention/compression; the controller owns executed actions; the environment owns physical truth and subsequent observations. Latent memory must be scoped to embodiment, policy revision and episode reset, and it cannot overrule the low-level safety envelope.

benchmark_contract.workload: long-horizon robotic manipulation under partial observability
benchmark_contract.models: paper-defined VLA baselines and LaMem-VLA variants
benchmark_contract.hardware: training/inference hardware Not Disclosed sufficiently for reproducible latency comparison
benchmark_contract.length: task trajectories in SimplerEnv-Bridge and LIBERO; exact token/action-horizon distribution is benchmark-specific
benchmark_contract.concurrency: single-agent policy evaluation; multi-robot concurrency Not Evaluated
benchmark_contract.slo: No production control-frequency or safety SLO disclosed
benchmark_contract.evaluator: SimplerEnv-Bridge and LIBERO success metrics plus memory ablations
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Simulation/benchmark gains do not prove real-robot robustness, calibrated memory truth or safe latency under physical control.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports the dual-latent-memory mechanism and listed benchmark gains. It does not prove real-world safety, durable cross-session memory, recovery from contaminated state or general embodiment transfer.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch26 covers perception-action feedback, action chunks and hierarchical control, but lacks a clear contract for model-internal latent memory across a physical episode.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds a two-timescale policy-state branch and corrects ownership: latent VLA memory is action-conditioned episode state, not durable Agent memory.
books_review.suggested_patch: Near the latent predictive interface, add short/long latent policy state with curator-controlled promotion. Bind it to observation/action schema, embodiment, policy version, episode reset and staleness. State that environment observation and safety controller remain authoritative; use text/RAG memory only as a separate information-system handoff.

families.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07702v1#S3 — trajectory normalization and dependency graph
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07702v1#S4 — backward slice and root-cause candidate extraction
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07702v1#S4 — diagnosis comparisons
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07702v1#S5 — agent benchmarks and component studies; appendices
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07702v1#S5 — observational traces, parser/judge dependence and limited causal identification
families.mechanism_summary: STRACE converts noisy agent trajectories into typed dependency graphs, then slices backward from a failed outcome to isolate the minimal relevant action/observation chain and propose root-cause candidates. Structural compression improves diagnostic focus, but a graph reconstructed from observations remains evidence for dependency, not proof of intervention-level causality.
families.state_and_flow: The trace store owns immutable raw events; the parser owns typed nodes/edges; the slicer owns a derived dependency subgraph; the evaluator owns failure labels; a human or experiment owns causal confirmation. Optimization may consume diagnosed candidates only with provenance back to the raw trace.

benchmark_contract.workload: failure diagnosis and optimization over tool-using agent trajectories
benchmark_contract.length: benchmark trajectory lengths; distribution Not Disclosed consistently
benchmark_contract.slo: No production SLO; diagnosis accuracy/utility and optimization outcomes
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author agent benchmarks and judge/diagnosis protocol
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Reconstructed dependency plus benchmark agreement does not establish causal effect under intervention, and parser/judge errors can redirect the slice.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 and event-time code support the structural diagnosis pipeline and bounded benchmarks. They do not prove causal identification from observational traces or eliminate evaluator dependence.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch69 already contains the exact immutable trace -> dependency graph -> backward slice -> candidate root cause route and explicitly denies observational causality.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Event-time provenance and exact-v1 locators close the evidence receipt without changing the chapter's durable claim.
books_review.suggested_patch: No body patch. Keep repository commit and limitations in Review notes.

families.title: DeepSearch-World: Self-Distillation for Deep Search Agents in a Verifiable Environment
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07820v1#S3 — verifiable offline search world and scaffold teacher
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07820v1#S4 — rejection, evolving SFT and round-bounded asynchronous generation/training
evaluation_locators: arXiv:2607.07820v1#S5 and Appendix A-C — search benchmarks, training/runtime configuration and ablations
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07820v1#S5 — offline-world coverage, verifier dependence and transfer to live search
families.artifact_locator: No official public repository or uniquely versioned event-time environment/training artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: The method builds a deterministic offline search environment whose answers can be verified, uses a stronger scaffold to create and reject trajectories, then alternates self-generated data with SFT across explicit rounds. Generation and learning may overlap inside a round, but the round boundary freezes the policy/data contract before the next promotion.
families.state_and_flow: The offline corpus and tools own reproducible observations; the scaffold owns candidate trajectories; the verifier owns acceptance; the round manifest owns policy/checkpoint/data identity; the live workflow remains a separate mutable system. Distilled behavior inherits only what the offline world can express and verify.

benchmark_contract.workload: deep web-style search in an offline verifiable Wikipedia environment
benchmark_contract.models: Qwen3.5-9B learner with scaffold/teacher models as specified
benchmark_contract.hardware: one 8-GPU NVIDIA H20 node for training and a two-node H20 generation/training setup
benchmark_contract.length: maximum training sequence 32,768; up to 30 agent steps
benchmark_contract.batch: round-specific; exact normalized global batch is paper-defined
benchmark_contract.concurrency: asynchronous generation/training across the reported H20 topology
benchmark_contract.slo: No live-search SLO; task accuracy and training efficiency
benchmark_contract.evaluator: paper deep-search benchmark suite with deterministic offline tools/verifiers
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Offline reproducibility does not prove live-web freshness, tool reliability or open-world correctness. Verifier gaps become training blind spots.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports the offline data-factory and round-bounded self-distillation pipeline on listed search tasks. It does not validate live search safety or make the offline world a production workflow substitute.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch81 already has the exact 'Offline World is a verifiable data factory, not a Live Workflow substitute' route with round manifests and transfer boundaries.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: The full v1 adds benchmark fields and limitations but no uncovered durable mechanism.
books_review.suggested_patch: No body patch. Retain source details in Review notes and preserve the offline/live authority boundary.

families.title: Linear Attention Architectures: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Cross-Layer Routing
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S2 — unified recurrent notation across linear-attention families
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S3 — CLER cross-layer routing
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S4 — CLVR representation alignment
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S5 — controlled architecture and optimizer comparisons
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07953v1#S6 — routing ablations and scaling runs; Appendix A-B
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07953v1#S7 and S9 — single-run routing gains, scale attenuation and absence of inference benchmarks
families.mechanism_summary: A common recurrent form exposes where DeltaNet/GDN/Kimi-like architectures differ in decay, update and gating rather than treating names as incomparable systems. Cross-layer error routing fails when a write residual is injected into a basis that does not share its representation; CLVR first projects the write value into an aligned hidden stream, making the added route semantically compatible.
families.state_and_flow: Each layer owns recurrent state and a representation basis; the optimizer/training stack owns the learned frontier; cross-layer routing owns an explicitly transformed signal. A residual may cross layers only after its state space and scale are aligned, and reported architecture quality must remain bound to optimizer, learning rate and stack pattern.

benchmark_contract.workload: controlled language-model pretraining and downstream evaluation of linear-attention families
benchmark_contract.models: 350M comparison suite plus 1.3B/3B and 15B-token scaling studies
benchmark_contract.batch: global batch 128 in the controlled setup
benchmark_contract.concurrency: distributed training across four GPUs; serving concurrency Not Evaluated
benchmark_contract.slo: No inference SLO; validation loss and downstream task quality
benchmark_contract.evaluator: author controlled pretraining/downstream suite; routing experiments are primarily single runs
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: Architecture rankings change with optimizer, learning rate and hybrid stack. CLVR gains diminish at scale and no serving benchmark proves runtime advantage.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports a controlled comparison and the aligned-routing mechanism. It does not establish a universally best linear-attention architecture or production inference advantage.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch22 explains recurrent/linear-attention state and Gated DeltaNet, but does not yet make representation-basis alignment a condition for cross-layer state routing or bind comparisons tightly enough to the training stack.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds two durable corrections: a cross-layer signal must be transformed into the receiver's state space, and 'architecture quality' is inseparable from optimizer, learning rate and layer-mixing contract.
books_review.suggested_patch: After the Gated DeltaNet branch, add a short cross-layer routing subsection: raw write error is not portable across representation bases; route an aligned value/hidden signal through a learned, initially neutral projection. In the comparison checklist, bind every linear-attention result to optimizer, LR, stack pattern and inference contract; do not declare a universal winner from the single-run routing gains.

families.title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S3 — Kronecker-factored Hessian and bidirectional incoherence
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S4 — Hessian-trace mixed precision
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S5 — calibration, perplexity and downstream quality
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07964v1#S6 — bit allocation, latency and ablations; Appendix A-E
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.07964v1#A6 — calibration overhead, temporary gradient-covariance memory and runtime comparison boundaries
families.artifact_locator: https://github.com/Intelligent-Computing-Lab-Panda/KronQ is disclosed, but GitHub history contains no commit at or before the Daily window cutoff; event-time implementation provenance is Not Verified.
families.mechanism_summary: KronQ approximates second-order weight sensitivity as output-gradient covariance Kronecker activation covariance, then uses two-sided incoherence transforms and Hessian-trace sensitivity for mixed-bit allocation. After preprocessing, the output-gradient factor cancels from the column update algebra, but it still influences the transformed representation and layer sensitivity decision.
families.state_and_flow: Calibration owns activation and output-gradient statistics; the quantizer owns transformed weights and bit allocation; the build artifact owns scales/codebooks/layout; the serving engine owns executable kernel compatibility. Accuracy evidence about a quantized artifact is separate from latency evidence about a concrete runtime/kernel.

benchmark_contract.workload: post-training weight-only LLM quantization and batch-1 latency
benchmark_contract.hardware: NVIDIA A100; 70B BF16 uses two GPUs while W4 uses one GPU in the reported latency comparison
benchmark_contract.length: calibration uses 128 WikiText2 samples of length 2048; latency sequence contract varies by table
benchmark_contract.concurrency: single-stream latency; online serving concurrency Not Evaluated
benchmark_contract.slo: No production SLO; perplexity, downstream accuracy, calibration time and latency
benchmark_contract.evaluator: WikiText2 perplexity and paper downstream suite
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: The 70B BF16-versus-W4 hardware count is not apples-to-apples. Calibration adds roughly 8-11 seconds per layer and temporary H_G memory, and accuracy gains do not guarantee serving speed.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports the Hessian factorization, transforms and reported accuracy on listed LLaMA/calibration contracts. It does not prove general runtime speedups, event-time code equivalence or universal calibration transfer.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch49 discusses quantization as a build artifact and covers activation-aware/error-aware methods, but not output-gradient curvature as a separate sensitivity signal.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds a second-order branch where both input activation and output-gradient covariance shape the transformed quantization problem and mixed-bit allocation, while runtime speed remains a separate kernel contract.
books_review.suggested_patch: After activation-aware quantization, add a Kronecker-curvature branch. Explain H_G tensor H_X, two-sided preprocessing and trace-based bit allocation; note the later algebraic cancellation without pretending H_G was irrelevant. Separate artifact-quality evidence from executable-kernel latency, and preserve simpler activation-only methods when calibration memory/time dominates.

families.title: Can We Trust LLM's Logic? Quantifying Uncertainty, Coherence, and Robustness via a Graph-Based Framework
families.revision_relation: v1 owner event; no later revision is used for claims
method_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08017v1#S3 — causal-DAG decomposition and semantic-structural graph distance
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08017v1#S4 — medoid and GRCS uncertainty features
evaluation_locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08017v1#S5.SS1 — five-benchmark and model/decomposer contract
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08017v1#S5.SS4 — adversarial-medoid ablations; Appendix B-C
limitations_locators: arXiv:2607.08017v1#S7 — short reasoning horizons, decomposer/judge dependence, scale attenuation and computational cost
families.artifact_locator: No official public repository, graph corpus or uniquely versioned event-time artifact is disclosed in exact v1.
families.mechanism_summary: GraphEVAL samples multiple chains of thought, uses a separate deterministic decomposer to turn each into a claimed causal DAG, and compares semantic/structural graph distance. A graph medoid and GRCS features measure agreement and robustness; an adversarial-medoid intervention tests whether the selector merely follows a central but wrong trace.
families.state_and_flow: The generator owns sampled text; the decomposer owns derived graphs; the embedding/distance function owns pairwise geometry; the medoid selector owns representative choice; external labels or executable checks own correctness. Graph consistency is a sensor and must not be converted directly into a truth probability.

benchmark_contract.length: 20 CoT samples per question, temperature 0.7, reasoning graphs of roughly 3-6 steps
benchmark_contract.slo: No serving SLO; uncertainty ranking, coherence and robustness
benchmark_contract.evaluator: GSM8K, BoolQ, StrategyQA, MedQA and GPQA; GPT-4o decomposer and Qwen3 embedding model
benchmark_contract.generalization_warning: The raw graph score is not a calibrated probability. Results weaken on larger models and depend on the decomposer, embedding and short-horizon graph contract.

families.claim_boundary: Exact v1 supports graph-structure agreement as an additional uncertainty signal and its listed ablations. It does not prove logical truth, calibrated confidence or robust decomposition for long/open-ended reasoning.

books_review.existing_proposition: Ch66 separates confidence signals from factual correctness and requires calibration against external evidence, but focuses on token/sample agreement rather than topology of derived reasoning.
books_review.new_evidence_delta: Adds reasoning-graph topology as a distinct sensor while preserving the authority boundary: coherence across derived DAGs can rank uncertainty but cannot own truth.
books_review.suggested_patch: In the uncertainty-sensor section, add graph-structured agreement after sample consistency. Bind the score to decomposer, embedding, graph-distance and sample contract; require calibration against labels, tools or executable evidence. State explicitly that a coherent graph medoid may still be consistently wrong and that raw GRCS is not a probability.
